deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft from Riemann's natural-philosophy fragment on gravitation and light. In it, gravity and light are both explained by the motion of a continuous 'Raumstoff' (space substance, an aether). The previous page set up a variational principle for aether displacements eta with the constraint div eta' = 0 and a multiplier lambda. The next page treats the Dirichlet-type uniqueness argument for V - U, where U = ∫dm/r.

Part I: gravity (top of the page).
(a) The gravitational force is determined by a potential function V. The force components are X_i = ∂V/∂x_i (sign convention: force = +grad V).
(b) V is fixed by two conditions.
  1) ΔV dx1dx2dx3 = 0 outside the attracting bodies. For each ponderable element it has an invariable value, ΔV dx1dx2dx3 = -4π dm. Here dm is the attracting mass that attraction theory assigns to the element. In modern form this is Poisson's equation ΔV = -4πρ.
  2) If all bodies lie in a finite region, then r ∂V/∂x_i -> 0 as r -> ∞, measured from a point of that region. This is a decay condition at infinity.
  [Mine: with these conditions, Green's identity (used on the next page) gives V = ∫dm/r uniquely.]
(c) Physical interpretation. Riemann reads the sources -4π dm as aether flowing into ponderable bodies. Matter continually absorbs Raumstoff. Since the bodies do not change, the stuff must vanish there, so a cause acting inside ponderable bodies continually annihilates it. Outside ponderable bodies, all changes and motions of the space substance are to have their causes in the immediate neighbourhood. This is an explicit postulate of action by contact, rejecting action at a distance.

Part II: light, i.e. motions of the Raumstoff in empty space (heading 'c, ... im leeren Raume').
Let v = (v1, v2, v3) be the aether velocity. Write □ = ∂_t² - c²(∂1² + ∂2² + ∂3²).
  (1) div v = 0.
  (2) □(curl v)_k = 0 for k = 1, 2, 3: the rotation components ∂v2/∂x3 - ∂v3/∂x2, etc., each satisfy the wave equation with speed c.
  Riemann restates (2) as: □(v1 dx1 + v2 dx2 + v3 dx3) is a complete differential. That is, □v = grad φ for some scalar φ.
  [Mine: □ commutes with curl, so curl(□v) = □ curl v. Hence (2) ⇔ curl(□v) = 0 ⇔ □v is locally a gradient, by the Poincaré lemma on a simply connected region. Also div(□v) = □ div v = 0 by (1), so Δφ = 0.]
Riemann's conclusion: these are local hyperbolic PDEs. The motion at a point depends only on motions in the adjoining space- and time-elements, so the complete causes can be sought in the nearest surroundings (local, finite-speed propagation).

Part III: continuity.
Equation (1) confirms the earlier assumption that the density of the Raumstoff is unchanged in the space motion. (div v) dx1dx2dx3 dt expresses the amount of stuff flowing into the volume element in time dt. Since this is 0, the amount contained stays constant: incompressibility, with the continuity equation ∂ρ/∂t + div(ρv) = 0 and ρ constant.
errors: Sign slip in Part III: (div v) dV dt is the net OUTflow from the element, not the inflow (inflow = -div v dV dt). It is harmless here because the quantity is 0.
In the 'oder' line the operator is written ∂_t² - cc ∂x1² + ∂x2² + ∂x3² without brackets. It must be ∂_t² - c²(∂x1² + ∂x2² + ∂x3²), as in the three equations above.
The step from (2) to 'complete differential' holds only locally or in a simply connected region. Riemann asserts the equivalence without comment ('wie sich leicht ergibt'), but it is standard.

Physically: in empty space div v = 0, yet at ponderable bodies Part I requires sinks. The draft does not reconcile these here, though it is consistent if (1) is restricted to empty space, as the heading indicates.

Condition 2 (r·∂V/∂x -> 0) is weaker than needed for the usual Green's-identity uniqueness proof, which uses V = O(1/r) and grad V = O(1/r²). It suffices with the potential normalised to vanish at infinity, but the normalisation is not stated.

results.what: Gravitational potential characterised by ΔV = -4πρ (0 in vacuum) and a decay condition at infinity, so V = ∫dm/r.
results.modern_name: Poisson equation / Newtonian potential boundary-value characterisation

results.what: Gravity interpreted as aether continuously flowing into and being annihilated in ponderable matter (sink model), with the postulate of contact action outside matter.
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Nachlass 'Gravitation und Licht', published in Werke 1876); similar ideas in Euler and later Bjerknes/Hicks

results.what: Light as an incompressible aether flow with div v = 0 and the wave equation for curl v; equivalently □v = grad φ, i.e. □(v·dx) is an exact differential.
results.modern_name: Transverse vector wave equation (vorticity obeys the wave equation); gauge-like formulation □A = grad φ
results.usually_credited_to: Elastic-aether theories of MacCullagh (1839), Cauchy, Green; Riemann's own version is in his published Nachlass fragment

results.what: Continuity equation: div v dV dt is the net flux, so div v = 0 means constant density.

deep.surprise_reason: This page is a draft of Riemann's known natural-philosophy fragment on gravitation and light, printed in his Gesammelte Werke (Nachlass, 1876). It contains the gravitational potential conditions, the aether-sink interpretation, and the equation □(v1dx1 + v2dx2 + v3dx3) = complete differential. The mathematics (Poisson equation, wave equation for curl, continuity equation) is standard for the period. The ideas are already attributed to Riemann and discussed by historians.

checkable.sympy: x,y,z,t,c=symbols('x y z t c'); v=[Function('v%d'%i)(x,y,z,t) for i in (1,2,3)]; box=lambda f: diff(f,t,2)-c**2*(diff(f,x,2)+diff(f,y,2)+diff(f,z,2)); simplify(box(diff(v[1],z)-diff(v[2],y)) - (diff(box(v[1]),z)-diff(box(v[2]),y)))==0
checkable.asserts: □ commutes with curl components, so □ curl v = curl □v and (2) ⇔ curl(□v) = 0 ⇔ □v locally a gradient.
□ commutes with div, so with div v = 0 any φ with □v = grad φ is harmonic.
V = m/r is harmonic outside the mass (condition 1 in vacuum).
r·∂V/∂x -> 0 at infinity for the Newtonian potential (condition 2).
A gradient field grad φ has zero curl (the 'complete differential' direction of the equivalence).

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'deren Comp. grad. dieß gibt' is doubtful; the sense is 'bestimmt, derart daß ∂V/∂x1, ∂V/∂x2, ∂V/∂x3 die Componenten der Schwerkraft sind'.
End of condition 1: 'durch den Bezeichnung werden soll' should read approximately 'u. durch dm bezeichnet werden soll' (the mass element dm, used on the next page as -4π dm).
Condition 2: 'muß daher werden' is better read 'unendlich klein werden' / 'muß ... unendlich klein werden'.
'oder' line: restore the brackets, (∂_t² - cc(∂x1² + ∂x2² + ∂x3²))(v1dx1 + v2dx2 + v3dx3) = einem vollständigen Differential.
'c, Erzeugung [?] (der) lineare Erscheinungen' is uncertain; possibly 'Erzeugung der Lichterscheinungen im leeren Raume'. This would match the light theme, but the image is too faint to confirm.
Final sentence: 'und da die in ihm enthaltene Stoffmenge bleibt daher constant' is better construed as 'und die in ihm enthaltene Stoffmenge bleibt daher constant'.
